bio: I'm Sirpreet (Siri) Dhillon, a systems and AI engineer with a BASc in Computer Engineering from Simon Fraser University. Since 2019 I've worked independently, designing and shipping software and AI solutions for small businesses and individual clients, from requirements through production.

My background runs from hardware to the cloud. I've designed bio-amplifier circuits in an SFU research lab, built FPGA graphics cores, automated testing at Ford, and engineered medical-imaging pipelines in the FAISAL lab. Today I build LLM applications and agents, and I'm developing a SAR processing pipeline designed to run on TPUs aboard satellites.
I work best embedded with a team: understanding the real problem, building the thing, and staying until it works in production.

currentWork.title: SAR processing on edge TPUs, in orbit
currentWork.summary: Radar satellites spend most of their downlink budget sending raw synthetic-aperture radar data to the ground, where it waits hours to be processed. I'm building an open pipeline that focuses and analyzes the raw radar signal onboard, on a TPU, so the satellite sends back answers instead of raw data.
points: NumPy range-Doppler reference (range compression, RCMC, azimuth compression) that matches theory: 2.65 m measured vs 2.66 m expected range resolution
JAX port of the focusing chain for TPU execution, exportable as an onboard artifact
Real-world foundations: a Sentinel-1 scene over Galveston Bay with precise orbits and AIS ship tracks for maritime detection
